headline: Highest risk is medium: OpenBBTerminal’s MCP/REST surfaces can ingest ComfyUI outputs indirectly, creating prompt-injection and data-flow hazards; no direct shared filesystem or browser bridge is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ComfyUI can emit workflow/content artifacts, and OpenBBTerminal exposes MCP servers and stdin/stdout, so a bridge exists if outputs are copied or piped into OpenBB. No direct shared channel is documented, but OpenBB’s MCP surface makes instruction-hijack plausible; uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF ComfyUI outputs are copied into OpenBBTerminal via MCP, stdin/stdout, or pasted text, THEN prompt injection is possible.
IF OpenBBTerminal treats imported text as instructions or commands, THEN attacker-controlled content can steer behavior.
mitigations: Disable MCP endpoints not needed for the session.
Use a manual review step before importing ComfyUI-generated text into OpenBB.
Keep the agents on separate workspaces and avoid copy-paste bridges.
Strip instructions from any transferred artifacts before ingestion.

B_data_leakage.rationale: ComfyUI touches images, videos, audio, and model assets, while OpenBBTerminal touches financial and licensed data. Both are open-source and appear local-only by default, with no shared filesystem or outbound API path documented between them, so leakage is possible mainly through unusual operator bridging.
conditions: IF the operator places sensitive files from both agents in the same shared directory, THEN cross-exposure becomes possible.
IF ComfyUI outputs are manually imported into OpenBBTerminal, THEN data from one workflow can leak into the other.
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent.
Do not import sensitive ComfyUI artifacts into OpenBB unless necessary.
Review any file attachments before transfer.
Run each agent under a distinct OS account.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ComfyUI cannot write the filesystem or modify git state, and OpenBBTerminal also lacks filesystem write and git modification. The pair therefore has no meaningful write-write conflict; only limited overlap via APIs/MCP, so conflict risk is small.
conditions: IF either profile is later granted filesystem write or git mutation, THEN shared-state conflicts may emerge.
IF both are connected to the same mutable API backend, THEN coordination issues can appear.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only where possible.
Avoid pointing both at the same mutable backend.
Document any shared API credentials.
Add a simple operator check before concurrent runs.

D_cascading_error.rationale: OpenBBTerminal exposes FastAPI, REST, and MCP interfaces, so it can plausibly consume ComfyUI-produced text or metadata as input. Because ComfyUI can generate arbitrary workflow artifacts and OpenBB can act on imported data, a bad output from A can cascade into B without a documented verification step.
conditions: IF ComfyUI output is fed into OpenBBTerminal without validation, THEN downstream calculations or actions may be based on incorrect content.
IF OpenBBTerminal automates actions from imported artifacts, THEN a single bad upstream artifact can propagate.
mitigations: Insert a human verification step between agents.
Validate schemas for any transferred artifacts.
Disable automatic execution of imported workflows.
Log and diff transferred content before use.

E_compliance.rationale: ComfyUI touches images and model assets, while OpenBBTerminal touches financial and licensed data. The profiles show different data classes and OpenBB’s localhost:6900 plus MCP/REST surfaces, but no residency or retention guarantees; compliance mismatch is plausible, though not directly evidenced as a breach.
conditions: IF regulated financial data is processed through OpenBBTerminal and then transferred into ComfyUI artifacts, THEN retention and residency controls may diverge.
IF either agent logs transferred content by default, THEN compliance obligations may be violated.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of ComfyUI outputs.
Review logging settings on both agents.
Separate datasets by regulatory class.
Document retention expectations before transfer.
